title: Season Roundtable: What We Got Right and Wrong

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Hello and welcome to the season roundtable. I'm Maya Torres. Today we go back through the claims our guests made this season and check how they held up.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena
transcript.text: Thanks, Maya. Happy to be graded in public.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Same here. Some of my takes aged better than others.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Let's start with remote work. GitLab still runs as an all-remote company and publishes its company handbook publicly at handbook.gitlab.com.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: That handbook is the single source of truth for how GitLab works. Team members find answers asynchronously instead of waiting for a meeting.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com and Tumblr, has been fully distributed since it was founded in 2005.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Doist, the maker of Todoist and Twist, is remote-first and async-first, with people spread across dozens of countries.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Gallup's surveys of remote-capable US employees show hybrid as the most common arrangement, at roughly half of workers.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: About a quarter of remote-capable US workers are fully remote according to Gallup, and the rest are on site.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena
transcript.text: Return-to-office mandates will push hybrid below a third of remote-capable workers by 2030.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Atlassian moved to a distributed model called Team Anywhere in 2020 and kept it after the pandemic.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Lena, healthcare. The FDA maintains a public list of AI-enabled medical devices, and it now lists more than 1,000 authorized devices.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena
transcript.text: The FDA reviews those devices through its standard premarket pathways, which are 510(k), De Novo and PMA.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena
transcript.text: Hospitals use AI to read X-rays and CT scans and to flag urgent cases so clinicians review them first.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: In April 2018 the FDA authorized IDx-DR through the De Novo pathway as the first autonomous AI diagnostic system.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena
transcript.text: IDx-DR is now sold as LumineticsCore by Digital Diagnostics, and it screens for diabetic retinopathy without a specialist reading the image.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Symptom-checker and triage chatbots from Ada Health and Buoy Health are offered to patients online.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena
transcript.text: A 2019 study in Science by Obermeyer and colleagues found that a widely used care-allocation algorithm underestimated the needs of Black patients.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena
transcript.text: That algorithm used past health costs as a proxy for health needs, which is how the bias got in.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: McKinsey estimated in 2021 that telehealth use had stabilized at levels 38 times higher than before the COVID-19 pandemic.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena
transcript.text: Investment in digital health also surged during the pandemic, with record venture funding in 2021.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena
transcript.text: AI will replace radiologists in most hospitals by 2035.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Medicare covered more than 50 million telehealth visits in 2020, up from a few million in 2019.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Sam, startups. Raising venture capital means selling equity, so each priced round dilutes the founders' ownership.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Investors in a priced round typically receive board seats and protective provisions, which reduces founder control.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Venture capital funds usually have a life of about ten years, so investors need a liquidity event within that window.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Bootstrapping means funding a company from savings and customer revenue, so founders keep full ownership and control.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Mailchimp bootstrapped for about twenty years before Intuit bought it for roughly 12 billion dollars in 2021.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Basecamp has stayed profitable and independent since 2004 without taking venture capital for growth.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Seed rounds in 2025 were smaller than in 2021 because investors shifted money into AI startups.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Space next. NASA's Mars Sample Return was meant to launch around 2026, but it has been delayed and restructured and has not launched.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena
transcript.text: NASA's Perseverance rover landed in Jezero Crater on February 18, 2021, and has been caching rock samples for a future return.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Perseverance carried the Ingenuity helicopter, which made the first powered flight on another planet in April 2021.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: No humans have landed on Mars, and NASA's Moon to Mars planning puts the first crewed missions no earlier than the late 2030s.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: SpaceX will land humans on Mars before 2030.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Markets. Bitcoin's highest price in 2025 was about 126,000 dollars, set on October 6, 2025.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Bitcoin did not reach 200,000 dollars in 2025, so that prediction from our spring episode was wrong.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: On October 29, 2025, Nvidia became the first public company to reach a market capitalization of 5 trillion dollars.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Nvidia's data center revenue passed its gaming revenue in 2023 because of demand for AI chips.

transcript.speaker: Sam
transcript.text: Apple reached a market value of 3 trillion dollars in January 2022, the first company to do so.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena
transcript.text: My prediction from last season about telehealth holding steady looks right so far.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: That's the roundtable. Thanks to Lena and Sam, and thanks for listening.
